The '''Galaxies Opera House''' was a prestigious theater located in the upper levels of the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Owned and operated by [[Romeo Treblanc]], the business was in part funded by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who received a heavily-secured [[Palpatine's private viewing box|private box]] in exchange. The [[Opera/Legends|opera]] house was designed as an alternative to the [[Coruscant Opera/Legends|Coruscant Opera]], a favorite of wealthy [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] families during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

==History==
This opera house was favored by [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] over the [[Coruscant Opera/Legends|Coruscant Opera House]] frequented by his [[Finis Valorum/Legends|predecessor]].<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Because of his patronage, and his gracious donations, the Supreme Chancellor received a [[Palpatine's private viewing box|private viewing box]] within the upper stories of the main theater.<ref name="Treblanc DB" />

A pivotal meeting between [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was held here, in which Palpatine told Anakin the story of [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis the Wise]] and brought Anakin a step closer to joining the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. During this meeting, important dignitaries watched an acrobatic performance by a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] group of the opera [[Squid Lake/Legends|''Squid Lake'']].<ref name="ROTS" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Continuity===
The Galaxies Opera House was first alluded to by the "A Night at the Theater" entry in [[Episode III Set Diary]], a [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] on [[August 23]], [[2004]], in which it was called the "Galaxies Theater."<ref name="Set Diary">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20040823.html|series=Episode III Set Diary|text=A Night at the Theater}}</ref> The opera house then appeared and was identified as the Galaxies Opera House by the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of the final film of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]], [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], written by [[Matthew Stover]]<ref name="ROTS-N">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> and released on [[April 2]], [[2005]]<ref name="ROTS-N release">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=30059|text=Matthew Woodring Stover}}</ref> ahead of the opera house's appearance in the film itself<ref name="ROTS" /> on [[May 19]] of that year.<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref>

The Galaxies Opera House appeared in the [[2006]] non-[[canon]] comic ''[[Tag & Bink: Revenge of the Clone Menace]]'', written by [[Kevin Rubio]], with the performance of ''Squid Lake'' seen in ''Revenge of the Sith'' spoofed with the Mon Calamari ballet dancers replaced by characters from the film [[Wikipedia:Finding Nemo|''Finding Nemo'']].<ref name="Tag & Bink">''[[Tag & Bink: Revenge of the Clone Menace]]''</ref>

===Conception===
{{Quote|During rehearsal, I said, 'My God, this is a four-page scene&mdash;I've had five scenes in the Chancellor's office already&mdash;how am I going to do this?' So I put it in an opera house, watching a ballet&mdash;''Squid Lake''&mdash;which worked out great.|George Lucas, on the creation of the Galaxies Opera House.|<ref name="ArtOf">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>}}
The scenes in ''Revenge of the Sith'' featuring Palpatine's recounting of the Tragedy of Darth Plagueis were originally conceived as taking place in the [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|Chnacellor's office]]. However, director [[George Lucas]] believed that too many scenes in the movie had taken place there, and called art department supervisor [[Fay David]], who in turn contacted concept artist [[Ryan Church]] and had him create four illustrations for an opera house.<ref name="ArtOf" /> Church came up with the idea of a giant anti-gravity water ball<ref name="AWN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.awn.com/vfxworld/otherworldly-concept-designs-ryan-church|text=Otherworldly Concept Designs of Ryan Church|author=Wollf, Ellen|date=2005-07-13|archivedate=20220514013510}}</ref> and designed the look of the opera<ref name="ArtOf" /> which became known as ''Squid Lake'' in a reference to the real-world ballet ''[[Wikipedia:Swan Lake|Swan Lake]]''.<ref name="AWN" /> Due to the spherical balls of water, the opera house was designed spherical on the exterior<ref name="ArtOf" /> and later took on a 360-degree design, with the opera stage at the center of the theater.<ref name="SW Archives">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]''</ref> Actor [[Ian McDiarmid]], who played Palpatine in ''Revenge of the Sith'',<ref name="ROTS" /> had a previous background in theater which made Pablo Hidalgo believe that the theater setting was fitting.<ref name="Set Diary" />

[[File:OperaBoxMiniature-SWCTP.png|250px|right|thumb|ILM created a practical model of the opera's viewing box, where the rest of the structure was rendered on blue-screen.]]

The opera box which Palpatine and Skywalker sat in was blue-screened except for the chairs themselves, designed by [[Lucasfilm]]'s art department. The surrounding box's features were later built<ref name="SWCTP" /> by [[Industrial Light & Magic]]'s model shop as a practical miniature.<ref name="ArtOf" /> Similarly, the corridor scene featured in the film was shot entirely on blue-screen.<ref name="SkywalkerSage">''[[Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' &mdash; [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]: "ILM Episode III Siggraph Reel"</ref> The exterior scene, featuring a sixty foot long, twenty foot wide blue ILM-built staircase<ref name="Set Diary" /> was filmed at [[Shepperton Studios]] as part of additional photography on [[August 23]], [[2004]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> The blue of the set was then replaced by a 3D matte painting of the environment, and the scene featured over fifty extras with reused background alien masks changed to feature jewelry and makeup.<ref name="Set Diary" />

Concept art for the operagoers was designed by [[Sang Jun Lee]], and after the first sketches Lucas asked for the dresses to become "sexier, formal, [and] more glamorous." Jun researched formal costumes from the [[Wikipedia:Middle East|Middle East]], [[Wikipedia:Turkey|Turkey]], [[Wikipedia:Russia|Russia]], and [[Wikipedia:Mongolia|Mongolia]], as Lucas wanted different cultures to be seen in the opera scenes. Concept art for opera limousines were made by Ryan Church.<ref name="ArtOf" />
